The verifier: diag = rows - 1 = 15. Red cells must satisfy r + c == 15. So the diagonal is the anti-diagonal from (0,15) to (15,0). Red cells lie on this diagonal. Find min row s, length l. Old reds set to 7 (orange... wait, 7 is orange in ARC, 2 is red). Yes.

New length new_l = l+1; new_s = s - new_l. Then place red at r = new_s + i, c = diag - r = 15 - r, for i in 0..new_l-1, within bounds.

Important: note the natural language says background is orange (7) and red (2). The verifier sets old reds to 7 and draws new ones.

Also important: if new_s < 0, cells are clipped (out of bounds skipped). So the new line may be clipped.

Also note: verifier checks reds with r+c==15 only. So the line always lies on the main anti-diagonal of the 16x16 grid.

Contiguous anti-diagonal segment: positions (s, 15-s), (s+1, 14-s), ..., (s+l-1, 16-s-l). Since c = 15 - r, contiguous rows means contiguous anti-diagonal cells.
